why: Both analyses land on specialist instrument selling, budgets and goals, and both wrongly rule out implants, but Analysis 2 puts ending flat-salary sales and founder-family control in its top three stop-doing items and sets an explicit annual net-earnings growth bar, which is closer to the key's march. Analysis 1's headline brutal fact (70% beds with no one selling) matches the key more directly, but its verdict is less tight and it buries the sales-pay fix lower in its list.
